findings.title: Data quality score improved significantly
findings.statement: The dataset quality score increased from 57.1 out of 100 to 98.5 out of 100 after cleaning 8 clips.
findings.recommendation: Use the cleaned dataset for training as the quality score is now high.

findings.title: Class imbalance persists after cleaning
findings.statement: The dataset remains imbalanced with a largest to smallest class ratio of 2.0, where 'yes' has 10 clips and 'stop' has 5 clips.
findings.recommendation: Apply data augmentation or oversampling techniques to the 'stop' class to improve model robustness.

findings.title: Label mismatches identified
findings.statement: Transcription analysis flagged 3 clips where the audio content does not match the folder label.
findings.recommendation: Manually review and reassign or remove the 3 flagged mislabeled clips before training, as this is a critical blocking issue that will cause model degradation.

findings.title: Dataset contained duplicates and corrupt files
findings.statement: Initial cleaning removed 1 corrupt file, 1 exact duplicate, and 1 near-duplicate file.
findings.recommendation: Continue monitoring for duplicates if new data is added to the dataset.

findings.title: Audio quality issues removed
findings.statement: Cleaning removed 1 silent, 1 too short, 1 clipped, and 2 noisy clips that were unsuitable for training.
findings.recommendation: Ensure future data collection follows strict quality guidelines to avoid these common audio defects.

findings.title: Dataset size is extremely small
findings.statement: The dataset size after cleaning is extremely small with only 23 clips total, which is insufficient for training a robust keyword-spotting model.
findings.recommendation: The current dataset size is insufficient for training; the model will likely overfit or fail to generalize. Collect additional audio samples for all classes before attempting to train.

findings.title: Inconsistent audio formats
findings.statement: The dataset contains mixed sample rates (16kHz and 44.1kHz) and channel counts (mono and stereo) across the 23 clips.
findings.recommendation: Standardize all audio files to a uniform sample rate (e.g., 16kHz) and channel count (mono) as a mandatory preprocessing step in the model pipeline.

narrative.headline: Dataset quality improved to 98.5 but remains insufficient for model training.
narrative.executive_summary: Cleaning efforts increased the dataset quality score from 57.1 to 98.5 by removing 8 unsuitable clips, including corrupt, silent, and noisy files. Despite these improvements, the final set of 23 clips is too small to train a robust keyword-spotting model. Furthermore, the dataset suffers from a 2.0 class imbalance ratio between 'yes' and 'stop' labels and requires manual verification for 3 flagged mislabeled clips. The current volume of data is inadequate for reliable performance.
next_steps: Perform manual verification of the 3 flagged mislabeled clips.
Source additional audio data to address the extremely small sample size of 23 clips.
Implement data augmentation or oversampling to mitigate the 2.0 class imbalance ratio.
Standardize all remaining files to a uniform 16kHz mono format to ensure consistency.
